explain: With I we always use am: I am, you are, he/she/it is. Example: I am happy.

notes.is: Is goes with he, she or it: She is a student.
notes.are: Are goes with you, we and they: You are a student.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word first: I can be a student.

explain: With he, she or it we use has, not have. Example: Tom has a cat.

notes.have: Have goes with I, you, we and they: I have two brothers.
notes.haves: There is no word 'haves'. The -s form of have is has.
notes.having: Having needs is/are first, and we don't use it for family.

explain: They takes are: we are, you are, they are. Example: They are my friends.

notes.is: Is is for one person or thing: He is from Spain.
notes.am: Am only goes with I: I am from Spain.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word: They will be in Spain.

explain: Use an before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u). Example: an egg, an orange.

notes.a: A goes before a consonant sound: a banana. Apple starts with a vowel.
notes.two: Two needs a plural word: two apples.
notes.many: Many needs a plural word too: many apples.

explain: We ask about a name with What. Example: What is your name? – I'm Lily.

notes.Who: Who asks about a person: Who is she? – My sister.
notes.Where: Where asks about a place: Where is your bag?
notes.When: When asks about a time: When is your birthday?

explain: With I, you, we, they the 'not' word is don't. Example: I don't like rain.

notes.doesn't: Doesn't is for he, she, it: She doesn't like coffee.
notes.not: We can't say 'I not like'. We need don't.
notes.no: No goes before a noun: I have no coffee.

explain: For things he/she/it does often, add -s to the verb. Example: She reads every day.

notes.play: Play is for I, you, we, they: We play football.
notes.playing: Playing needs is: He is playing now.
notes.is play: We don't say 'is play'. Every Sunday = present simple: plays.

q: There ___ three cats in the garden.
explain: There are for more than one thing; there is for one. Example: There are two dogs.

notes.is: There is is for one thing: There is one cat.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word: There will be three cats.

explain: On means touching the top of something. Example: The cup is on the desk.

notes.at: At is for a point or place: at school, at the door.
notes.to: To shows movement: I go to the park.
notes.from: From shows where something starts: a letter from Gran.

explain: After can, use the plain verb with no -s, no -ing and no to. Example: I can sing.

notes.swims: No -s after can: we say 'Can he swim?', not 'swims'.
notes.swimming: No -ing after can: 'Can you swimming?' is wrong.
notes.to swim: No 'to' after can: 'Can you to swim?' is wrong.

explain: These means more than one, so the noun is plural. Example: These are my socks.

notes.shoe: Shoe is just one. These needs more than one: shoes.
notes.a shoe: A shoe is one shoe. These needs a plural.

explain: Questions with you/I/we/they and a normal verb start with Do. Example: Do you like cats?

notes.Does: Does is for he, she, it: Does she like ice cream?
notes.Are: Are goes with adjectives or -ing: Are you happy?
notes.Is: Is goes with he/she/it: Is it cold?

explain: Use in with months, years and seasons. Example: in June, in winter.

notes.on: On is for days and dates: on Monday, on 5th May.
notes.at: At is for clock times: at six o'clock.

explain: Look! means it is happening now, so use is + -ing. Example: Look! It is raining.

notes.sleep: Sleep is for I/you/we/they and for habits, not now.
notes.sleeps: Sleeps is for habits: The baby sleeps a lot.
notes.are sleeping: Are is for more than one. One baby takes is.

q: This is Tom. ___ is my friend.
explain: Tom is a boy, so we use he. Example: This is Sam. He is nine.

notes.She: She is for a girl or woman.
notes.It: It is for a thing or an animal.
notes.They: They is for more than one person.

explain: Yesterday is past. The past of are is were (we were, they were). Example: We were happy.

notes.was: Was is for I, he, she, it: I was at home.
notes.is: Is is now and for one person.

q: ___ is my bag? I can't find it.
explain: Where asks about a place. Example: Where is the cat? – Under the bed.

notes.What: What asks about a thing: What is this?
notes.Who: Who asks about a person: Who is that?
notes.How: How asks about the way or feelings: How are you?

explain: With he, she, it the 'not' word is doesn't. Example: He doesn't like rain.

notes.don't: Don't is for I, you, we, they.
notes.isn't: Isn't goes with adjectives: She isn't happy. Like is a verb.
notes.not: We can't say 'She not like'. We need doesn't.

explain: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so we use an. Example: an ice cream.

notes.a: A is for consonant sounds: a bag, a hat.
notes.some: Some is for 'more than one' or 'a bit of': some milk.
notes.two: Two needs a plural: two umbrellas.

q: The cat is ___ the box. You can't see it!
explain: In means inside something. Example: The pencil is in my bag.

notes.on: On is on the top. Then you could see the cat!
notes.at: At is for a place point: at the door.
notes.of: Of is not used for where things are.

explain: We ask about the clock with What time. Example: What time is lunch? – At one.

notes.How many: How many asks about a number of things.
notes.What day: What day asks about Monday, Tuesday...

explain: Now means use are/is + -ing. They takes are. Example: They are playing.

notes.watch: Watch is for habits: They watch TV every day.
notes.is watching: Is is for one person. They needs are.

explain: Use at with clock times. Example: at nine o'clock, at noon.

notes.in: In is for months and years: in May.
notes.on: On is for days: on Friday.
notes.to: To shows movement, not a time.

q: This is my brother. ___ name is Leo.
explain: His shows something belongs to a boy. Example: Sam and his dog.

notes.Her: Her is for a girl: my sister and her name.
notes.He: He is the person, not 'belonging to him'. We need his.
notes.Its: Its is for a thing or an animal.

q: How ___ is your grandma? She's seventy.
explain: We ask about age with How old. Example: How old are you? – I'm eight.

notes.many: How many is for counting things.
notes.much: How much is for amounts and prices.
notes.big: How big asks about size, not age.

q: There ___ a dragon in the story.
explain: One thing takes there is. Example: There is a cat on the bed.

notes.are: Are is for more than one: There are two dragons.
notes.be: Be needs a helper word first.

q: I can ___ my name in English.
explain: After can, use the plain verb. Example: She can write.
Questions with he/she/it and a normal verb start with Does. Example: Does he like fish?

notes.Do: Do is for I, you, we, they.
notes.Is: Is goes with adjectives or -ing, not 'have'.
notes.Has: Has is not used to start this question. Say 'Does she have'.

explain: Those means more than one, so use are. Example: Those are my shoes.

notes.is: Is is for one: That is my pencil.

q: Sam was tired, ___ he went to bed.
explain: So shows a result: what happened because of it. Example: It was cold, so I wore a coat.

notes.but: But shows a surprise or difference: tired, but he played.
notes.because: Because gives the reason, not the result: He went to bed because he was tired.
notes.or: Or gives a choice: tea or milk?
